newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy adviser sees 25 trln lire 98 budget - paper.
newsitem.headline: Italy adviser sees 25 trln lire 98 budget - paper.

text.p: Italy would need a deficit-cutting budget of at least 25 trillion lire ($14.5 billion) in 1998 to secure a place in the European Union's planned single currency, an economic adviser to Prime Minister Romano Prodi was quoted on Sunday as saying.

Paolo Onofri, who chaired a study group set up by Prodi on reforms to the welfare state, told La Repubblica newspaper he believed that around 15 trillion lire of the total should come from spending cuts.
But he said the cuts need not all be reductions in spending on health and pensions, arguing that savings from restructuring the state railways and postal services could be significant.

"I believe that to put Italy in a secure position the budget must be of at least 25 trillion lire. The challenge we are facing is to achieve 15 trillion lire of cuts in primary spending," Onofri told the paper.

Prodi has drawn up deficit-cutting measures of some 77 trillion lire for 1997, mainly through revenue-raising steps, to try to keep Italy's deficit this year to the 3.0 percent of gross domestic product required for single currency membership.
The European Commission and the International Monetary Fund have forecast that Italy could just exceed the target this year but will clearly overshoot in 1998.

The 1998 forecasts have raised the stakes as Prodi prepares to tackle reforms to welfare spending in the face of resistance from trades unions and the hard left Communist Refoundation party, which secures his parliamentary majority.
Onofri argued in the interview that structural changes to the pensions system were vital. But he said such changes were required over the long term.
"The pensions problem must not be read as a figure to be written into the 1998 budget," Onofri said.

"The issue is not to save a few hundred billion lire straightaway but to give the (financial) markets the certainty that Italy's pensions system is heading towards a situation of balance in the long term".
He said the railways and posts systems were areas where savings could be made through rationalisation and cost cutting that had so far not been pursued adequately.
"The government could say to the unions 'do you want 15 trillion lire of cuts to pensions spending or do we want to see if there are other sectors that can help us to save?'," he said.

The 1998 budget has to be presented to parliament by the end of September and passed into law by the end of the year. Prodi has said its contents will reflect welfare state reforms, which he hopes to begin tackling in May.
